author: Swarajya Staff
title: CBSE Re-Evaluation Portal Remains Operational Despite Major Cyber Attack, Over 56,000 Applications Processed
text:
Tech
Swarajya Staff
Jun 04, 2026 | Updated 09:08 AM GMT+5:30

The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) successfully thwarted a major 3. 8-million-packet denial-of-service cyber attack on its re-evaluation portal on Wednesday (3 June) afternoon, while processing over 56,000 student applications by 9.30pm.
The board confirmed that its technical teams remained vigilant throughout the incident, implementing real-time security measures to maintain uninterrupted service for students.
The attack represented the latest in a series of cyber security challenges facing the portal since its launch on 2nd June.
Earlier this week, malicious actors attempted to disrupt services through multiple attacks, including a denial-of-service assault that generated 1.5 million hits within two minutes and more than one lakh unauthorised file access attempts.
The board implemented Aadhaar-based verification to strengthen security protocols.
Application numbers showed a sharp rise from Tuesday night, when the portal had recorded 28,000 successful submissions by 10pm.
More than 400,000 students accessed scanned copies of their evaluated answer books this year, double last year's figure of approximately 200,000.
The surge follows concerns amongst Class 12 students regarding answer-book discrepancies and marking irregularities.
Four public sector banks—State Bank of India, Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and Indian Bank—processed more than 56,000 payment transactions through their gateways.
SBI alone handled over 40,000 payments, while Bank of Baroda reported more than 7,500 transactions.
The shift to multiple banking partners followed a security incident involving unauthorised manipulation of fee amounts on HDFC Bank's payment gateway.
CBSE extended the application deadline until 6 June for verification, photocopying answer sheets, and re-evaluation.
Students can apply by paying Rs 100 per answer book for photocopying and Rs 25 per question for re-evaluation.
The board stated that technical teams continue monitoring portal performance and introducing refinements to ensure a smoother experience for students.
